chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

O Allah, I seek Your protection from that You make my outward appearance good in the gleam of eyes, and make ugly what I conceal from You as my inner self, guarding against the admiration of people for myself with all that You are aware of from me, so I show to people the beauty of my appearance and I disclose to You the evil of my deeds, seeking nearness to Your servants and remoteness from Your pleasure.

key_terms.رِثَاءِ النَّاسِ: admiration of people / being regarded with esteem

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of seeking protection from making one's outward appearance good while concealing inner distance from God?
ai.summary: This supplication from Nahj al-Balagha articulates the subtle danger of 'hidden hypocrisy' (riya'), where the believer fears that their outward piety pleases the masses while their inner state remains distant from God's pleasure. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on aligning both the apparent (zahir) and the hidden (batin) with divine will, ensuring that acts of worship are purely for Allah rather than for social validation or human admiration.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 276. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

O’ my Allāh, I seek Your protection from this that I may appear to be good in the eyes of the people whilst my inward self may be sinful before You, and that I may guard myself (from sins) only for show before the people although You are aware of all about me. Thus, I appear before the people in good shape although my evil deeds are placed before You. This means achieving nearness to Your creatures but remoteness from Your pleasure.
